data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central diagnostic criterion fails its own internal logic: it claims that clustered panel errors on cases where the checklist is silent indicate mere compliance with an incomplete checklist, but its own countercondition ("the expert's intuition is also anchored to the same incomplete set of features") shows that error clustering on unchecklisted features cannot distinguish a checklist-specific compliance failure from a generic feature-omission failure shared by both systems. If the expert also fails those cases, the checklist is not causally incomplete in a way that privileges expert intuition—yet the claim treats such clustering as evidence that "the reliability gain is merely compliance with an incomplete proxy," presupposing the expert would succeed. The transferred diagnostic rule is therefore question-begging: it assumes the expert uses additional causally relevant features (the very point at issue) to license the inference from error clustering to "mere compliance."
